# Result: the F/015–016 predictions against the arrows

The predictions are `docs/predictions/f015-f016-arrows.md`, committed (c4277ea)
before the arrows were read. The arrows were then transcribed by a reader who
was not shown the predictions or the audit (`sources/notes/F015-F016-arrows.md`;
no person has checked it). Scored here by hand, row by row; nothing in the
prediction file has been changed.

**A gap in the prediction file.** It was generated by a script from the label
table, and the script missed the two stacked labels of F/015 band 1 ("U 7"
over "B 5" in Axis B, "U 9" over "B 3" in ′S1). So 42 motions were
predicted, not 44. Only the 42 are scored. (Both missed ones moved as P would
have it: ↑ .4 and ↑ 1.1.)

## Rule 1: motion (direction and lift)

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Predicted motions | 42 |
| Direction right | 42 (one reading uncertain: F/015 band 4 ′R, "[?↑] 1.1") |
| Direction wrong | 0 |
| Lift written exactly as predicted | 38 |
| Lift written with the right digits but no point ("6", "2", "4", "4" for .6, .2, .4, .4) | 4: F/015 band 2 ′S′S, band 3 Axis B, band (5) Axis B; F/016 band 4 Axis C |
| Lift with the wrong digits | 0 |

Under the rule as committed, a figure without its point is a miss, as it was
for F/018's "6" (`f-bu-audit.md`). So: **42/42 directions, 38/42 lifts; the
four misses are figures written without a point, none with a wrong digit.**
Where a struck figure was flagged (F/015 ′R bands 2 and 4), the motion follows
the figure written after it.

## Rule 2: return at row "11–1/3" of the same band

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Testable (the band's returns are on the sheet) | 30 |
| Return by a double-headed arrow at 11–1/3, as predicted | 18 (F/015 bands 2 and 4) |
| Return at row 12 instead | 3 (F/015 band 3) |
| No return transcribed in the band | 7 (F/016 band 2) |
| A double-headed arrow at row 12 that does not match the motion | 2 (F/016 band 2: Axis B, ↓ .4 then ⇊ .2; ′S′S, ↓ .6 then ⇊ with no figure) |
| Untestable (F/015 band (5) ends after row 1; F/016 band 4 is cut off) | 12 |

**Rule 2 failed as stated: 18 of 30.** It was taken from F/013, where every
labelled part returns at 11–1/3.

**Seen after the test, not a prediction.** On F/015 the platforms alternate:
in bands 2 and 4 they return at 11–1/3, in bands 1 and 3 platforms 3–10
return at row 12 and 1–2, 11–12 at 15–1/3. The three parts that return at row
12 are in band 3, on platforms 3, 6 and 3. So "a part returns when its
platform returns" fits all 21 of F/015's testable returns. That rule was not
committed before the arrows were read, so it is a hypothesis for a further
test, not a result. It does not explain F/016 band 2, where most parts show no
return at all and two show a double-headed arrow that does not match their
motion.

## Rule 3: no row-1 motion for a lone U

23 columns with only a U label in a band (18 on F/015, 5 on F/016): none has
an arrow in row 1. **23/23.**

## Also seen

- Arrows with no label: F/015 band 1 ″P (↑ .6); F/016 band 1 ″P (↑ .6) and
  band 3 ″p″p (↑ 1.1); F/016 band 3 ′S1, ′S2 and ′R (↓ "6", ↓ .6, ↑ with no
  figure) under faint traces in the 2/3 row that may be erased labels. P makes
  no prediction for them.
- F/016's platform 11–12 return in its carried-over band 0 is a ⇊ (down), the
  opposite of the ⇈ every other band gives them.

## Reading

The motion rule held on a sheet it had not seen: every predicted direction,
and every predicted lift up to a missing point. The fixed return row did not:
the return depends on the band, and on F/015 it follows the platforms' own
returns, which is what P would say if it had been stated that way. F/016 band
2 is not explained by either.
